text:
maria-dev: Quick sync — noticed 2 sessions drifted from eu-west to us-west during the canary on Sat. Not total outage but some writes landed in the wrong region for tenants with residency requirements. Who wants to own an ops playbook + short-term mitigations? :eyes:

ashwin-arch: Ugh. I saw traces too. Likely interaction of routing fallback + concurrent lease swap. Short term: disable fallback for residency-tagged tenants and force local-only reads/writes. Long term: we need a graceful soft-demote handshake + explicit residency affinity in the API.

kevin-sre: I can own the runbook. Short-term checklist I propose:
- roll back canary to previous release
- temporarily block cross-region fallbacks for tenants with consent_flag = true
- run anti-entropy job to reconcile writes (read-after-write check)
I'll add alerts for increased cross-region write rate and >5% placement anomalies.

olivia-privacy: Please make the tenant-level flag mandatory for enterprise customers who opted-in for data residency. We should avoid opaque heuristics that move writes. Also we need audit logs flagged with region_of_final_write.

ranjit-platform: Agreed on both. For API-level hints I suggest adding a header and a routing hint: "X-Resident-Region: eu-west-1" and a token-level copy of residency policy. Example config snippet for our edge router: 
```json
{"route_policies": {"prefer_local": true, "resident_region": "eu-west-1", "fallback_allowed": false}}
```
That should be a short-term guardrail until we implement soft-demote.

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary v2026.03.18-8 started by @maria-dev at 2026-03-14T01:12:08Z :white_check_mark:

maria-dev: Ranjit — can we make router honor the header immediately as a feature flag per env? If yes, Kevin can flip it for prod tenants.

ranjit-platform: Yes, I can toggle a feature-flag in edge for headers by EOD. We'll default to off for public tenants. Need list of enterprise tenant IDs to lock down.

kevin-sre: I'll produce the list and include instructions in the runbook for toggling. Also adding an emergency circuit-breaker to prevent cross-region write surge: if cross_region_write_rate > 0.5% of traffic for a tenant over 5m, automatically pause fallback and mark tenant in investigation mode.

ashwin-arch: Circuit-breaker + soft-demote = good. For the long-term design here's a sketch of safe soft-demote handshake we should RFC:
1) origin region marks session as 'demoting' and writes a demote-intent lease with TTL
2) target region sees intent and waits for grace-window (prefetch/pause) then signals acknowledgement
3) origin drains in-flight requests, flushes KV cache for that session, and revokes lease
4) target promotes lease and accepts writes
This avoids blind split-brain and gives operator hooks.

olivia-privacy: Add requirement that if tenant has residency_enforced = true, step 2 must include an operator approval or automated consent check against tenant policy. No auto-promote.

maria-dev: Nice. Kevin/Ranjit/Kevin: please coordinate runbook + header flag + alerts. Ashwin + Olivia: can you turn the soft-demote sketch into an RFC doc (short) — include failure modes and metrics to observe (e.g., in-flight kv misses, lease collision rate, time-to-settle).

ashwin-arch: I'm on RFC. I'll include a failure-mode matrix and sample k8s operator hooks. Expect first draft in 2 days.

kevin-sre: Runbook staged, will post link here once done and schedule a 30m ops walkthrough.

ranjit-platform: Feature-flag change queued, will test in staging after kevin posts tenant list.

maria-dev: Great — priority: stop any more accidental region-writes for residency tenants, then iterate on the soft-demote RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
